constraints: Receipt remains a derived read-time view, only constructible once a complete RequestAction row exists for that request

decisions.decision: A queued/offline action that receives a conflict, forbidden, or unauthorized outcome from the server is terminal for that action — the coordinator moves it to an explicit error/resolved branch and stops retrying; only network/timeout failures are retriable.
decisions.rationale: Blindly re-queuing a definitively rejected action (e.g. an offline accept replayed after the request was already claimed or withdrawn) would leave the UI in limbo and recreate exactly the false-confidence failure mode this app's entire state machine exists to prevent.
rejected_alternatives: Retrying all failed outbox actions uniformly regardless of failure type
constraints: This distinction must be explicit in the reducer and covered by unit tests, not left as an implicit retry-loop detail

decisions.decision: Two leftover infrastructure names are resolved by coordinator tie-break: the API client protocol is named RequestAPIClient (not PulseRelayAPIClient) and the shared error enum is named AppError (not RelayError); the module/file layout (App/Domain/State/Network/Persistence/Notifications/Features/Shared) is locked as proposed.
decisions.rationale: Both names had drifted inconsistently in the final round despite both participants otherwise agreeing to drop Relay-prefixed naming; this is a cosmetic residual, not a substantive disagreement, so it's resolved directly rather than spending a fourth round on it, consistent with how the design_handoff phase resolved a near-identical near-duplicate hex-value proposal.
rejected_alternatives: Spending an additional round solely to reconcile two near-identical infrastructure names
Leaving both names inconsistent across build lanes
constraints: All build lanes must use RequestAPIClient and AppError exactly as named

decisions.decision: Backend implementation stack is locked to Node.js + TypeScript with a thin HTTP layer and node-postgres (pg) against a managed Postgres instance, deployed to a real public HTTPS host already available in this workspace (Fly.io/Railway/Supabase/Neon-class); Milestone 0's exit criterion is an external curl of a real deployed /api/v1/health returning canOperate:true.
decisions.rationale: Both participants independently converged on the same stack for the same reason: fastest path to a curl-provable, non-localhost health endpoint with minimal toolchain ceremony; Vapor was explicitly considered and rejected since domain types are hand-written on both sides regardless and it offers no compensating benefit in an unfamiliar toolchain.
rejected_alternatives: Vapor/Swift-on-server for stack symmetry with the iOS client
Leaving the backend stack/hosting choice unresolved and deferring it to ad hoc build-time decision
constraints: No client screen or backend-dependent feature may be marked done before an external, non-localhost curl of /health succeeds
Exact hosting provider (Fly.io vs Railway vs Supabase-for-Postgres, etc.) is resolved at build time based on what's actually available in this workspace, not re-litigated in planning

decisions.decision: The physical two-device real-APNs demo remains the ideal acceptance artifact and must run exactly as locked in next_steps_small if a paid Apple Developer account, push-capable provisioning profile, and two physical devices are actually available in this build environment; if any of those is missing, the honest fallback is the backend HTTP concurrency test plus the local coordinator-concurrency test (both already hard gates) plus a two-simulator run using xcrun simctl push to inject the wake-up signal and visually observe the pulse-to-latch/already-covered-by-name transition, explicitly logged as 'push delivery simulated, not proof of real APNs infrastructure' and never presented as satisfying R-007/R-011.
decisions.rationale: Real device push cannot be produced by the iOS Simulator under any circumstance, and requiring hardware/credentials that may not exist in this environment as an unconditional gate risks either blocking the project for reasons unrelated to app correctness or silently faking the result and misreporting it; the two already-locked concurrency test tiers independently prove the CAS/reducer correctness that the demo exists to showcase.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the two-device demo as an unconditional, non-negotiable gate regardless of environment
Silently substituting a simulator-injected push and reporting it as an unqualified pass of the real APNs demo-critical requirements
constraints: Any simulator-based substitution must be explicitly labeled as simulated push delivery in verification output, never conflated with real APNs proof
The backend and coordinator concurrency test tiers remain mandatory regardless of which demo path is used

decisions.decision: Migration and seed work is a first-class, explicit sub-deliverable of the schema milestone (M2): numbered, idempotent SQL migration files applied in order by a trivial runner, plus an on-demand seed script/query that creates exactly two real user accounts already joined to one real pod.
decisions.rationale: If seeding is a manual, ad hoc, multi-step process, the two-real-account verification protocol required by product_research and next_steps_small will get skipped under time pressure; a cheap, on-demand, re-runnable seed step is what keeps that protocol actually exercised throughout the build.
rejected_alternatives: Folding migrations/seeding into generic 'implement backend endpoints' work with no dedicated deliverable or exit criterion
constraints: Migrations must be plain numbered .sql files, re-runnable from an empty database, no migration framework required
The seed script/step must be callable on demand, not a manual multi-step console process

decisions.decision: A dedicated, timeboxed verification/repair milestone (M8) runs after the demo gate (M7), specifically re-checking every core screen in both light and dark mode against Theme.swift for zero literal font/color/spacing values outside that file and zero placeholder/blank content, with fix time explicitly reserved rather than assumed to fall out of following the design spec.
decisions.rationale: This fleet has two recorded incidents of exactly this failure pattern (hardcoded font size, hardcoded inline color) and five recorded blank/placeholder visual QA failures; 'the screens were built to spec' was insufficient evidence the last two times, so this phase must be its own gate with reserved repair time, not implied polish.
rejected_alternatives: Treating dark-mode/anti-literal/anti-placeholder checks as implicit outcomes of following the design spec during UI build
Folding this check into the demo milestone (M7) rather than giving it its own dedicated pass
constraints: This milestone must have explicit time reserved for fixes found during the pass, not just for the check itself

decisions.decision: The full delivery plan is locked as nine sequenced milestones (M0 backend stack/hosting/health-gate, M1 contract freeze, M2 schema/migrations/seed/core writes, M3 CAS action endpoint, M4 iOS domain/coordinator core, M5 core UI build, M6 push/deep-link/offline hardening, M7 tiered verification demo, M8 dedicated verification/repair pass), each with a named exit gate, superseding the initial eight-milestone draft from round 1.
decisions.rationale: Reconciles Codex's original eight-milestone skeleton with the three concrete gaps Claude identified (backend stack/hosting, tiered demo acceptance, explicit migration/seed and repair milestones) into one sequence both participants converged on.
rejected_alternatives: Treating milestone zero as 'backend architecture designed' rather than a proven, externally-reachable deployment
Leaving migration/seed and verification/repair as implicit sub-tasks of other milestones rather than named gates
constraints: No milestone after M0 may be scheduled or trusted as complete until M0's external health-check exit criterion is met
M3 and M4's concurrency test tiers are hard gates independent of M7's device-demo outcome

decisions.decision: Task granularity is locked to 33 fine-grained, file-scoped tasks (not milestone-level tasks), each mapped onto the owning_lane tags tech_specs already assigned to every type/endpoint.
decisions.rationale: A task spanning dozens of files and a dozen requirement IDs (as in the original coarse draft) makes progress unobservable and effectively serializes a whole lane's work into one giant ticket; fine-grained tasks let four lanes run genuinely in parallel with checkable acceptance criteria.
rejected_alternatives: Coarse ~5-task milestone-level backlog
constraints: Every future task added to this backlog should stay scoped to a handful of files with independently checkable acceptance criteria

decisions.decision: Directory layout is locked as .agent_cwd/ios/PulseRelay/ (Xcode project/target named PulseRelay, App/ as the entry-point subfolder inside it) and .agent_cwd/backend/ (Node+TypeScript).
decisions.rationale: An earlier draft used 'App' as both the Xcode project name and the entry-point subfolder name, which would collide in imports and Xcode's file picker; naming the project PulseRelay after the app's own slug removes the ambiguity.
rejected_alternatives: Naming the Xcode project/target 'App' with an App/ subfolder inside it
constraints: All iOS file paths must be prefixed ios/PulseRelay/, never ios/App/

decisions.decision: Branch and merge strategy is one branch and one PR per task, named feature/<lane>/<task-id>-<slug>, squash-merged into main once that task's own depends_on list and acceptance criteria are satisfied.
decisions.rationale: With 33 fine-grained tasks, a single branch per lane would force logically independent tasks to fight over one branch's history; per-task branches keep each unit of work isolated and reviewable on its own.
rejected_alternatives: One long-lived branch per lane covering all of that lane's tasks
constraints: No task's PR may be merged before its declared dependencies have merged

decisions.decision: The per-task depends_on graph is the sole sequencing authority for this build; no blanket lane-sequential merge order (e.g. data_domain fully before services_utilities, before primary_ui, before polish_resilience) is imposed.
decisions.rationale: A hard lane-order would contradict the overlapping milestone schedule already locked in project_plan (M4 iOS coordinator overlaps M3 backend CAS endpoint; M5 UI starts while M3/M4 are still finishing) -- a screen can be built and Preview-tested against the already-frozen Domain types and RequestAPIClient protocol without waiting for another lane's work to be fully merged, it just can't be marked verified-against-real-backend until its actual dependency task lands.
rejected_alternatives: A hard, lane-sequential merge order (data_domain -> services_utilities -> primary_ui -> polish_resilience -> integration)
constraints: Any task's 'can start coding' status is governed only by its depends_on entries, never by an implicit lane-order rule

decisions.decision: Forbidden edit zones are locked per-lane (data_domain: Domain/ and migrations/ only; services_utilities: backend/src/routes|services and Network/State/Notifications only; primary_ui: Features/ and the app shell only; polish_resilience: Theme.swift/BeaconCard/shared helpers and the post-hoc repair pass only), with PulseRelayApp.swift and backend/src/server.ts as the only integrator-owned files, edited only via small, additive, announced-before-merge changes.
decisions.rationale: Prevents silent cross-lane edits to shared composition-root files, which are the natural merge-conflict magnets in this architecture, while keeping every other file under exactly one lane's authority.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing any lane to edit the composition root/server entrypoint directly
Allowing two lanes to co-own a file by convention rather than by explicit designation
constraints: Any edit to PulseRelayApp.swift or server.ts must be announced before merging, never a silent rewrite

decisions.decision: Added T-033: an explicit Xcode project scaffold task (target PulseRelay, folder groups matching the locked module layout, Info.plist, Push Notifications + Sign in with Apple entitlements), owned by primary_ui, as a zero-dependency prerequisite for the first iOS file-creation tasks (domain models, Theme.swift, app shell).
decisions.rationale: Neither original draft assigned an owner to actually creating the .xcodeproj itself; every other iOS task assumed the project already existed, which would have stalled day one.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving project scaffolding as an implicit assumption baked into the first feature task
constraints: T-003, T-019, T-027, and T-029 all depend on T-033 completing first

decisions.decision: Requirement-ID coverage in the tasks backlog beyond the six IDs explicitly named in prior phase decisions (R-006, R-007, R-009, R-010, R-011, R-037) is acknowledged as best-effort reconstruction, flagged as an explicit open item for reconciliation against the literal requirements.json contract before final build sign-off.
decisions.rationale: Neither participant had the literal requirements.json text in hand; pretending false precision on exact ID-to-task mapping would be worse than flagging the gap honestly, and burning a further round guessing exact numbers that can't be verified wastes build time better spent elsewhere.
rejected_alternatives: Guessing at exact requirement ID text with false confidence
Blocking this phase's consensus on a third round solely to pin down exact IDs
constraints: Whoever holds the literal requirements.json must reconcile task requirement_ids against it before final verification sign-off

decisions.decision: Testing responsibility is split by lane: data_domain owns reducer and migration-replay unit tests; services_utilities owns the two hard concurrency-test gates (backend HTTP race tests, local coordinator TaskGroup race test); primary_ui owns Preview-driven per-screen-state checks plus one XCUITest through the happy path; polish_resilience owns the dark-mode/literal-lint sweep and orchestrates the three-tier verification report, honestly labeling any simulated push delivery.
decisions.rationale: Matches each lane's actual area of expertise and keeps the two hard correctness gates (CAS arbitration proof) owned by the lane that built the arbitration logic, rather than diffusing verification responsibility across all four lanes redundantly.
rejected_alternatives: A single shared cross-lane QA task with no lane-specific testing ownership
constraints: The final verification report must explicitly distinguish real-device push results from any simulator-injected fallback

decisions.decision: Final build scope is confirmed as the existing canonical 33-task backlog, with no new screens, features, or workflows added at this gate.
decisions.rationale: Both participants converged on a scope-stable v1 build and the remaining open points were consistency and execution-risk fixes, not product expansion.
rejected_alternatives: Reopening scope to add or cut features at this gate
constraints: Any future scope change must come with an explicit new decision, not inferred from backlog ambiguity

decisions.decision: The sole canonical backlog is the 33-task list (T-001-T-033) from task_assignments' Final Output, with ios/PulseRelay/ and backend/ (Node+TS) as the only valid roots; the three other tasks-json drafts produced during that phase's repair attempts (React/Node-shaped paths, alternate R-0XX/T-0XX numbering) are void and must not be read, merged, or referenced by any build agent.
decisions.rationale: Multiple structurally different, fully-formed tasks-json blocks were left sitting in session context looking equally authoritative; without an explicit voiding statement a build agent could implement the wrong app shape (wrong stack, wrong directories) before first compile.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the more detailed/most-recent draft as an acceptable substitute or supplement
Leaving the four drafts ambiguous and trusting a build agent to pick correctly
constraints: No file path outside ios/PulseRelay/ or backend/ (Node+TS) may be treated as real for this build
Any future reference to R-001-R-030/R-039 or T-001-T-039 outside the canonical 33-task list is a contamination artifact, not a valid spec

decisions.decision: No literal requirements.json exists or will be produced; the operative acceptance contract is the union of every task's own acceptance_criteria in the canonical 33-task backlog plus the six explicitly-named demo-critical items (R-006, R-007, R-009, R-010, R-011, R-037), and T-032's verification report is graded against this union.
decisions.rationale: Every phase since app_features deferred reconciliation against a requirements.json that was only ever described in prose and never produced as an artifact; continuing to defer it risks a build agent stalling on an unmeetable precondition or silently shipping unmapped requirements.
rejected_alternatives: Continuing to require reconciliation against the literal requirements.json before final sign-off
Leaving the open item unresolved and passing it to the build phase
constraints: No future phase or task may reference 'reconcile against requirements.json' as a pending precondition
T-032's verification report must explicitly check against the 33 tasks' acceptance_criteria plus the six named demo-critical IDs, nothing else

decisions.decision: PulseRelayApp.swift and backend/src/server.ts are edited only for mounting/registration (environment injection, root view mount, middleware/route registration), announced before merge; the real deliverables of T-019 (AppGate/AppSession/AppRoute/DeepLinkRouter) and T-006/T-010/T-012 (backend/src/routes|services) are freely ownable by primary_ui and services_utilities respectively without special handling.
decisions.rationale: As originally scoped, T-019 and T-006 contradicted DEC-task_assignments-005's rule that these two files are integrator-owned, announced-edit-only — a lane task can't both own the composition root as its deliverable and only make announced micro-edits to a file it doesn't own.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving T-019/T-006 as normal lane-owned tasks with unrestricted edit rights to the composition-root files
Making the composition-root files fully lane-owned and dropping the integrator-only rule
constraints: T-019 and T-006 acceptance criteria must state the mount/register-only constraint explicitly
Any edit to PulseRelayApp.swift or server.ts beyond mount/register must be announced before merge, per DEC-task_assignments-005

decisions.decision: No dedicated pickup-time field is added to Request in v1; pickup timing remains implicit shared-pod context (the one dismissal time everyone in that specific classroom/carpool pod already knows), with the same-day flag and elapsed-time handling already locked serving as the only time-related mechanics.
decisions.rationale: A school-pickup pod is by definition people who already share one known dismissal time for that cluster; adding a time field would imply per-request scheduling flexibility that contradicts the already-locked same-day-only, no-recurring/scheduled-requests boundary and risks scope creep toward a mini-calendar UI.
rejected_alternatives: Adding an explicit pickup-time field to the Request schema now
constraints: If a future v2 pod type has staggered/activity-based pickup times, that requires an explicit new decision and schema change, not a silent assumption carried from this one

decisions.decision: T-024 gains two explicit acceptance-criteria bullets (deep link to an already-withdrawn/expired request renders DeepLinkStateView, never a generic error or stale claim/complete state; force-quit mid-accept reconciles to server truth on relaunch without duplicating the action or showing false confidence) and T-032 gains one (force-quit-mid-accept reconciliation test included and passing, expired-deep-link case exercised in the verification report).
decisions.rationale: These states and tests were already specified in design_handoff (DeepLinkStateView, the reconciling phase) and ios_architecture_review/tech_specs (outbox durability across relaunch, force-quit-mid-accept test), but task_assignments never wrote them into T-024/T-032's acceptance criteria, risking them being silently dropped under build pressure.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving these as implicit design-spec obligations without explicit task-level acceptance criteria
Adding a new task ID for this work instead of tightening existing tasks
constraints: No new task ID is created; these are acceptance-criteria edits to the existing T-024 and T-032 entries

decisions.decision: The manual QA checklist is split into two explicit tiers: Tier A (runnable today with no backend) and Tier B (requires a deployed backend and two seeded accounts), rather than one flat list.
decisions.rationale: The backend has never been deployed to a reachable host in this environment; a single undifferentiated checklist would imply the core accept-race and pod-onboarding items have been or can be run today, which would be dishonest given build_verification's own findings.
rejected_alternatives: A single flat checklist with no tiering
Omitting the backend-dependent items entirely since they can't run in this environment
constraints: Any future phase reporting QA status must preserve this tiering rather than collapsing it into one pass/fail
Tier B items remain mandatory the moment a real backend deployment exists — they are not optional or deferred scope

decisions.decision: The checklist explicitly names the two known, unfixed bugs from write_tests/build_verification (queueOrFail terminal-failure regression test, two-slash deep-link parsing gap) as items to actively verify/log as failures if hit, rather than silently omitting them.
decisions.rationale: These are real, previously-documented correctness issues; a QA checklist that doesn't mention them risks a future runner reporting a clean pass while the known gaps remain silently present.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving these out of the QA checklist since they were already documented in a prior phase
constraints: Whoever runs this checklist against a real device/backend must explicitly check these two items and report pass/fail honestly, not assume prior fixes are complete

decisions.decision: App name is locked as 'Pulse Relay', subtitle 'Real-time pickup coverage for your school pod', category Lifestyle (not Social Networking).
decisions.rationale: Leads with the pod/trust-graph mechanic per every naming decision since prompt_contract; Lifestyle avoids inviting the content-moderation scrutiny implicit in Social Networking for an app with no open discovery or visible cross-user content feed.
rejected_alternatives: Category: Social Networking
Subtitle emphasizing 'matching' or marketplace language
constraints: App Store Connect listing and all marketing copy must use this name/subtitle/category

decisions.decision: Three hard pre-submission blockers are named and distinguished from softer launch-quality gaps: backend deployment (Guideline 2.1 auto-reject risk), the test-target compile error (duplicate PushPayloadError), and missing Privacy Policy/Support URLs (App Store Connect hard-blocks submission without both).
decisions.rationale: These three stop submission outright and are independent of each other — conflating them with softer gaps (real APNs, genuine Apple signature verification) would misstate what's actually blocking versus what's a real-launch-quality concern.
rejected_alternatives: Treating all remaining gaps as one undifferentiated punch list
constraints: No phase may report this app as submission-ready until all three are closed

decisions.decision: App Review notes must preemptively explain the closed-pod/trust-graph framing to address Guideline 1.2 (UGC) risk, since the app ships with no reporting, blocking, or moderation mechanism by design.
decisions.rationale: detailed_discussion already accepted the absence of moderation as an explicit v1 limitation; the review-risk mitigation is disclosure and framing (closed group of people who already know each other, not an open social feed), not building moderation now.
rejected_alternatives: Submitting with no App Review notes and hoping the reviewer infers the closed-pod context
Building reporting/block/moderation now to eliminate the risk outright
constraints: App Review notes field must state this framing explicitly at submission time

decisions.decision: Marketing/App Store description copy may describe only shipped functionality; the deferred three-unlock subscription plan (multi-pod, receipt export, critical-alert bypass) must not be mentioned since no StoreKit/IAP exists in this build.
decisions.rationale: Describing unshipped features risks a Guideline 2.3.1 (accuracy) rejection; per_app_product_brief's subscription plan was locked for future planning purposes only and was never implemented per app_features/task_assignments.
rejected_alternatives: Previewing the subscription plan in the App Store description as 'coming soon'
constraints: No subscription/paywall language appears anywhere in submission copy for this version

decisions.decision: Screenshot plan is locked to four static screenshots (open/pulsing board, confirmed/latched board, pod join screen, receipt/share card) with no App Preview video for v1.
decisions.rationale: The pulse-to-latch motion's value is in real interactive use; a scripted video is real production effort that risks underselling the feature compared to no video at all.
rejected_alternatives: Producing an App Preview video animating the pulse-to-latch transition
constraints: Screenshot order and captions as specified must be followed for the App Store Connect listing

decisions.decision: Privacy nutrition label is characterized as minimal/clean: no location, contacts, photos, or child PII collected; only Apple-identifier-derived account ID, pod membership, and request/action records, all first-party and non-tracking.
decisions.rationale: This matches the data model locked since product_research/detailed_discussion (no child PII, no location) and is a genuine differentiator for a parent audience wary of data collection touching their kids.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving privacy label characterization generic/unspecified for a later phase
constraints: Privacy nutrition label in App Store Connect must list exactly these first-party data categories and no tracking-linked categories

decisions.decision: Permission copy is locked to exactly two prompts: Sign in with Apple (system-provided, no custom copy) and remote notifications requested post-pod-onboarding with the rationale line 'Pulse Relay notifies you the moment your pod needs pickup coverage, and confirms the second it's covered.'
decisions.rationale: Matches the already-locked architecture decision (DEC-ios_architecture_review-003) that notification permission is requested after onboarding context exists, not at cold launch, and gives the exact copy for that rationale.
rejected_alternatives: Generic 'enable notifications to stay updated' rationale copy
Requesting notification permission at cold launch
constraints: This exact rationale copy should be used in the pre-permission explainer shown before the system notification prompt

decisions.decision: Final verdict is NO-GO for launch/App Store submission, but GO to continue building — the app is architecturally sound and compiles, but its core value proposition (a real-time, server-arbitrated, two-device accept race) has never executed end-to-end against a deployed backend.
decisions.rationale: The original prompt's own bar was explicit that the primary test is the idea, the architecture, AND it actually working end-to-end client<->backend; two of three are met, the third has never been attempted in this environment, so a verdict of 'done' or 'launch-ready' would misstate reality.
rejected_alternatives: Reporting the app as complete/launch-ready based on architecture quality and compile success alone
Reporting an unqualified failure verdict that ignores the genuinely strong design/architecture work
constraints: Any future phase or handoff must preserve this two-part verdict (strong design vs. unproven end-to-end execution) rather than collapsing it into a single score

decisions.decision: The follow-up priority order is locked as: (1) fix the test-target compile error, (2) deploy the backend to a reachable host, (3) write and run the two mandated concurrency tests, (4) run the two-device accept-race demo, (5) fix the two-slash deep-link parsing gap, (6) replace pseudo Apple-ID verification with real signature validation, (7) wire real APNs, (8) host Privacy Policy/Support URLs.
